description:
The verifAIed documentation, for you and for the user's questions.
**Free.** Call this whenever the user asks how something in verifAIed
works or how to do something with it, and whenever you are unsure what
a tool, a command, a gap or an error means.

Three ways to call it:

  - no arguments: the table of contents — every page with a one-line
    summary — and how to use the rest.
  - ``query``: the question, or a few words of it. Returns the
    sections that match best, each with its own text, so one call is
    usually enough to answer from. A hit marked ``truncated`` was cut
    short: read its page for the rest. Start here when you do not
    know which page holds the answer.
  - ``page``: one whole page as Markdown. Pass a name from the contents
    (the first page is ``overview``); a title or a documentation URL
    also works.

Pass ``page`` or ``query``, not both.

Answer from the returned text rather than from memory, and give the
user the page's ``url`` so they can read it themselves. A page with no
``url`` is one of the notes for agents: tell the user what it says,
there is no link to give. When nothing
matches, the documentation does not cover it: tell the user that, and
do not infer an answer from what is missing. Pages in the
group "For agents" are reference written for you and are not on the
website: ``agents/gaps`` (what every check_done gap means and what
closes it), ``agents/errors`` (what an error or refusal means and the
fix) and ``agents/formats`` (exact file and JSON formats, exit codes).

Every answer carries ``account``: the user's plan, and on the free
plan a note on what is refused, so you do not suggest a feature this
account cannot use. The table of contents has the full list of paid
tools.

This is the one tool that works with no account: a connection without
credentials can read the documentation, and its ``account`` is null.
Every other tool needs the user to sign in first.
name: docs
